free_tier.stated: 32 GiB maximum per project, and at most 10 unpublished projects per user. Both are config knobs (process.max_upload_size, services.upload_limit) rather than business limits, and they differ per deployment. Publishing requires at least one successfully parsed entry, and publishing is what frees the 10-project slot.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous for published entries via the NOMAD API and GUI.

record.tooling: Documented REST API requires HTTP authentication tokens for uploads via API endpoints. File parsers are plugin-based and format validation depends on target deployment configuration.
record.chaining: 10 unpublished projects × 32 GiB = 320 GiB of live scratch on a free account, and publishing an entry releases a slot. So the steady-state ceiling is bounded by how fast a human can publish, not by bytes.
record.limits_note: fails-quota at 32 GiB, and write-gated by the parser: 'A project must contain at least one successfully processed entry before it can be published.' Content must be materials-science-shaped (DFT codes, ELN exports) to be parseable at all. Both limits together make it useless as bulk storage despite the clean API.
record.reliability_note: Well-run EU (FAIRmat) infrastructure with a real API. The constraint is semantic, not technical.

evidence.proved: opened: 'a maximum project size of 32 GiB, controlled by process.max_upload_size'; 'at most 10 unpublished projects per user, controlled by services.upload_limit'; 'A project must contain at least one successfully processed entry before it can be published.'
